description.narrative:
The Cambodia–Thailand border has long been shaped by geopolitical tensions, historical disputes, and humanitarian crises. Spanning over 800 kilometers, this frontier has witnessed repeated cycles of displacement and conflict, particularly following the Cambodian civil war and the fall of the Khmer Rouge. Colonial-era boundary demarcations—especially around contested sites like Preah Vihear Temple—continue to fuel nationalist sentiment and military confrontations.
Since 25 July 2025, renewed violence near Preah Vihear hasdisplaced over 134,000 civilians, closed 600 schools, and triggered the return of 470,000 Cambodian migrant workers from Thailand. Despite a ceasefire on 28 July, instability persisted until the 8 August General Border Committee meeting in Malaysia, which led to a 13-point agreement and improved security along the border. Displacement has since declined, though some areas remain unsafe due tounexploded ordnance (UXOs), resulting in continued, localized displacement.
The conflict has also led to an unprecedented return of Cambodian workers from Thailand. As of 08 September 2025, the National Committee for Counter Trafficking reported 878,818 returnees. Many are young, underemployed, and formerly engaged in informal sectors such as construction, agriculture, hospitality, and manufacturing. This mass return presents a significant socio-economic challenge, with returnees facing immediate livelihood insecurity and limited access to formal employment or skills applicable in Cambodia.
To support long-term recovery and reintegration, it is essential to understand the profiles, vulnerabilities, and aspirations of these returnees. A rapid, evidence-based assessment will guidethe design of targeted programs—such as skills training, livelihood support, and economic reintegration—that respond to actual needs and promote resilience, poverty reduction, and environmental sustainability.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project#s implementation.
